Reference Attribute Table Target Layer Generator

Source: R/calibrate.R
geomorphon_targets.Rd

Derives aligned categorical raster layers from an integer ID raster and its Reference Attribute Table (RAT), with support for categorical columns and binned numeric columns. Attaches coverage statistics describing valid cell proportions and class counts.

Usage

geomorphon_targets(
  x,
  attrs = NULL,
  id_col = 1,
  vars = NULL,
  breaks = list(),
  labels = list(),
  right = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A single-layer categorical or integer SpatRaster.

attrs

Optional data.frame containing the attribute table. If NULL (default), the table is extracted from terra::cats(x)[[1]].

id_col

Column index or column name in attrs containing the keys that match raster values in x. Default is 1.

vars

Character vector of column names in attrs to convert into target raster layers. Default is all columns except id_col.

breaks

Named list of numeric break vectors for binning continuous attribute columns using base::cut().

labels

Named list of character vectors of category labels corresponding to breaks.

right

Logical. Indicating if the intervals should be closed on the right (and open on the left) or vice versa. Default is TRUE. Passed to base::cut().

Value

A multi-layer SpatRaster where each layer corresponds to a derived target variable with categories set via terra::levels(). The returned raster has an attached attribute "coverage", a tidy data.frame containing:

target

Target layer name.

n_total

Total number of cells.

n_valid

Number of valid non-NA cells.

n_na

Number of missing (NA) cells.

prop_valid

Proportion of valid cells (n_valid / n_total).

n_classes

Number of factor levels / distinct categories.

Examples

library(terra)
r <- rast(matrix(c(1, 2, 1, 3), nrow = 2, ncol = 2))
rat <- data.frame(id = 1:3, landuse = c("Forest", "Water", "Forest"), slope = c(12, 1, 25))
targets <- geomorphon_targets(r, attrs = rat, id_col = "id", vars = "landuse")
attr(targets, "coverage")
#>    target n_total n_valid n_na prop_valid n_classes
#> 1 landuse       4       4    0          1         2
